fields.name: units
fields.label: Units used in the month
fields.hint: The units (kWh) on your bill, or the difference between this month's and last month's meter reading.

fields.name: sanctioned_kw
fields.label: Sanctioned load
fields.hint: The kW printed on the bill; most homes are one to five. It sets the fixed charge. A connection of {{d.tou_threshold_kw|int}} kW or more is billed on peak and off-peak (ToU) rates instead: use the [[F13|ToU bill calculator]].

fields.name: protected
fields.label: Protected consumer
fields.hint: Tick if every one of your last six bills was within the protected unit limit; the bill usually prints the category.

fields.name: lifeline
fields.label: Lifeline consumer (up to one hundred units)
fields.hint: Lifeline rates apply only to very small consumers whose bill shows the lifeline category.

fields.name: period
fields.label: Billing quarter for QTA
fields.hint: The quarterly tariff adjustment depends on the quarter the bill falls in.

fields.name: fc_surcharge_per_unit
fields.label: FC surcharge
fields.hint: Financing cost surcharge per unit, from your bill. Secondary-source default; change it if your bill differs.
fields.placeholder: Blank = {{data.tariff.addons_secondary.fc_surcharge_per_unit.value|rs2}} per unit (none on lifeline or protected)

fields.name: fpa_per_unit
fields.label: FPA / FCA
fields.hint: Pre-filled with the latest NEPRA-verified fuel adjustment, the one for {{data.fpa_latest.fpa_for}} charged on {{data.fpa_latest.label}} bills. {{data.fpa_newest.note}} Replace it with the FPA rate printed on your bill (negative is a credit). Protected homes pay it too; lifeline bills carry none.

fields.name: fpa_units
fields.label: Units in the FPA month
fields.hint: NEPRA charges the FPA on the units of the month it adjusts (the FPA month, usually two months before this bill), not on this month's units. Copy that month's units from the units history on your bill. Blank = this month's units.

fields.name: gst_pct
fields.label: GST
fields.hint: Sales tax applied to the bill subtotal.

outputs.label: One unit past that limit adds

answer: An unprotected home using {{in.units|int}} units a month on a {{in.sanctioned_kw|int}} kW connection pays about {{out.total_rs|rs}}: {{out.energy_rs|rs}} in energy charges at {{out.rate|rs2}} per unit, plus the fixed charge, FC surcharge, QTA, the {{data.fpa_latest.fpa_for}} FPA and {{out.gst_pct|int}}% GST. Bill = units × slab rate + fixed charge + surcharges, then GST on the subtotal.
how: Energy ({{out.category}}): {{out.energy_calc}} = {{out.energy_rs|rs}}. Fixed charge for {{out.sanctioned_kw}} kW = {{out.fixed_rs|rs}}. FC surcharge = {{out.fc_rs|rs}}, QTA = {{out.qta_rs|rs}}, FPA = {{out.fpa_rs|rs}}. Subtotal {{out.subtotal_rs|rs}}; GST at {{out.gst_pct}}% = {{out.gst_rs|rs}}. Estimated bill {{out.total_rs|rs}}.
key_facts: An unprotected consumer pays the rate of the slab the monthly total reaches on every unit: {{out.units|int}} units are all charged at {{out.rate|rs2}}, giving {{out.energy_rs|rs}} in energy charges.

A protected consumer is billed slab-wise with the benefit of the lower slab, and the category needs every one of the last {{d.protected_months|int}} months at or under {{d.protected_max_units|int}} units.

The fixed charge is Rs per kW of sanctioned load and rises with the slab: a {{out.sanctioned_kw|int}} kW connection using {{out.units|int}} units pays {{out.fixed_rs|rs}} of it, and even a month with no units pays the lowest slab's {{data.tariff.unprotected.0.fixed_per_kw|rs}} per kW.

GST at {{out.gst_pct|int}}% is applied to the subtotal of energy, fixed charge and surcharges, which adds {{out.gst_rs|rs}} to a {{out.units|int}} unit bill; the surcharge and GST figures are from secondary sources and change monthly.

Lifeline rates apply only up to {{data.tariff.lifeline.1.upto|int}} units, with no fixed charge, and a connection of {{d.tou_threshold_kw|int}} kW or more is billed on a peak and off-peak (ToU) meter instead of slabs.

The bill jumps at {{out.cliff_units|int}} units: up to there every unit is billed at {{data.tariff.unprotected.6.rate|rs2}}, but one unit more moves all of them to the top slab rate of {{data.tariff.unprotected.7.rate|rs2}}, which adds {{out.cliff_rs|rs}} to the bill of an unprotected {{out.sanctioned_kw|int}} kW home.

Income tax is not in this estimate: under section 235 of the Income Tax Ordinance 2001, a home not on FBR's Active Taxpayers List pays advance income tax of {{data.tariff.addons_secondary.income_tax_235.rate_pct_non_atl|1}}% on a monthly bill of {{data.tariff.addons_secondary.income_tax_235.threshold_rs|rs}} or more; consumers on the list pay none.

formula.text: Bill = units × slab rate + fixed Rs/kW × sanctioned kW + (FC + QTA + FPA) × units, then + GST
lines: slab rate = unprotected: rate of the band the total reaches, on every unit
protected: units in each band at that band's rate (slab-wise)
fixed = Rs per kW for the band reached × sanctioned kW
FC = financing cost surcharge per unit; QTA = quarterly adjustment per unit; FPA = monthly fuel adjustment per unit
GST = percentage of the subtotal; lifeline has no fixed charge and no QTA

sections.h2: How does this electricity bill calculator work?
p: The calculator applies the NEPRA uniform A-1 domestic tariff for 2026, notified by the Government as SRO 279(I)/2026, which every DISCO ([[F2|LESCO]], [[F3|IESCO]], [[F5|GEPCO]], [[F6|FESCO]], [[F4|MEPCO]], [[F7|PESCO]], [[F8|HESCO]], [[F9|SEPCO]], [[F10|QESCO]], [[F11|TESCO]]) and [[F12|K-Electric]] charges; each name opens that company's own bill calculator. Enter your units, the sanctioned load from your bill and your category, and it shows the energy charge, fixed charge, FC surcharge, QTA, FPA and GST as separate lines, the way the bill prints them.

The energy and fixed rates were verified from the NEPRA tariff PDF. The FC surcharge, QTA, FPA and GST are from secondary sources, change monthly or quarterly, and whether GST applies to lifeline bills is still being verified (a real LESCO protected bill confirmed no FC surcharge on protected homes and GST on the whole subtotal, FPA included, with the FPA charged on the units of the month it adjusts); copy those lines from your own bill into the advanced fields for a closer match.

A protected consumer is a domestic consumer whose consumption stayed at or under {{d.protected_max_units|int}} units in every one of the last {{d.protected_months|int}} months, on a non-ToU connection below {{d.tou_threshold_kw|int}} kW. Protected rates are much lower and are applied slab-wise: the first hundred units at the first protected rate and the rest at the second.
The protected status is printed on the bill. The moment one month goes over the limit, the next bills are at the unprotected rates for every unit until a fresh run of six months under the limit.

Take your last six bills. If every one shows {{d.protected_max_units|int}} units or fewer and the connection is under {{d.tou_threshold_kw|int}} kW, tick the protected box; otherwise leave it clear. The difference is large: the worked examples below show the same {{d.protected_max_units|int}} units billed both ways.
A long billing cycle can push a normally protected home over the limit in one month. If your bill covers more than a month of days, check the reading dates before you accept the unprotected rate.

sections.h2: What is the bill for 200 units (LESCO or any DISCO)?
p: A {{d.protected_max_units|int}} unit bill depends almost entirely on the category. Protected, the units are billed slab-wise at the two protected rates; unprotected, all of them are at the second unprotected slab rate. The two worked examples below give both totals with the same fixed charge, surcharges and GST, and the reference table lists them side by side. For the typical bill at every step of units in every DISCO, see the [[bill-index|Pakistan Bill Index for this month]]; it prices every bill on a {{data.bill_index.sanctioned_kw|int}} kW sanctioned load, so its totals differ from a bill on another load.

sections.h2: What is the bill for 300 units?
p: {{out.units|int}} units is the default above: all units at {{out.rate|rs2}} = {{out.energy_rs|rs}}, plus {{out.fixed_rs|rs}} fixed charge for {{out.sanctioned_kw|int}} kW, {{out.fc_rs|rs}} FC surcharge, {{out.qta_rs|rs}} QTA, {{out.fpa_rs|rs}} FPA and {{out.gst_rs|rs}} GST, for about {{out.total_rs|rs}}. One unit over {{out.units|int}} moves every unit to the next slab, so {{out.units|int}} units is a line worth staying under.

mistakes: Billing slab-wise as an unprotected consumer. Unprotected bills charge every unit at the rate of the slab the total reaches, so one extra unit can raise the whole bill.
Ticking protected because this month is low. Protection needs all of the last six months under the limit; the bill prints the category.
Keeping the pre-filled FPA when your bill shows a different one. The monthly fuel adjustment can be a large positive or negative line; copy your bill's rate into the advanced field.
Using an old fixed charge. The fixed charge is per kW of sanctioned load and steps up with the slab, so a higher-usage month also pays a higher fixed charge.
Reading the estimate as the exact bill. Surcharge, QTA, FPA and tax values change monthly and some are from secondary sources; the estimate is for planning and for checking a bill that looks wrong.

faq.q: Is this electricity bill calculator updated for 2026?
faq.a: Yes. The slab rates and fixed charges are the uniform A-1 domestic tariff NEPRA set for 2026, verified from the NEPRA tariff PDF. The FC surcharge, QTA, FPA and GST are secondary-source values that change monthly, so copy them from your bill.

faq.q: Does this bill calculator work for every DISCO in Pakistan?
faq.a: Yes. LESCO, IESCO, GEPCO, FESCO, MEPCO, PESCO, HESCO, SEPCO, QESCO, TESCO and K-Electric all charge the same uniform domestic tariff; NEPRA sets one FPA for all of them as well, so the same units give the same estimate; real bills differ only by billing days, arrears and local items.

faq.q: Is there a WAPDA bill calculator?
faq.a: WAPDA no longer bills homes; its distribution side became the DISCOs, which all use the same NEPRA tariff. This calculator gives the same estimate people mean by a WAPDA bill calculator.

faq.q: What is the per unit rate of electricity in Pakistan?
faq.a: It depends on the slab and category. An unprotected home using {{out.units|int}} units pays {{out.rate|rs2}} per unit on every unit; lower slabs pay less and the top slab pays the most. Protected and lifeline consumers pay far lower rates. The reference table above lists the rate for each slab.

faq.q: What are the electricity slab rates in Pakistan?
faq.a: The unprotected domestic tariff has slabs of {{data.tariff.unprotected.0.upto|int}} units up to {{data.tariff.unprotected.6.upto|int}}, then one open-ended slab, each with its own rate and fixed charge. Protected consumers have two slabs up to {{d.protected_max_units|int}} units and lifeline consumers two slabs up to {{data.tariff.lifeline.1.upto|int}} units. The table above shows each slab's rate from the tariff file.

faq.q: What does protected consumer mean on my bill?
faq.a: It means your last {{d.protected_months|int}} months were all at or under {{d.protected_max_units|int}} units, so you are billed at the protected slab-wise rates. It is a status the DISCO works out from your history, not something you apply for.

A domestic consumer who used more than {{d.protected_max_units|int}} units in any of the last {{d.protected_months|int}} months, or has a ToU meter. Every unit is billed at the rate of the slab the monthly total reaches, with a higher fixed charge.

faq.q: Why is my actual bill different from this estimate?
faq.a: The FPA line, the exact FC surcharge and QTA for the month, TV fee or other local items, arrears and the number of days in the cycle all change the total. Enter the FPA and surcharge from your bill in the advanced fields for a closer estimate.
